## What the chronicles say [Record]

The Act of Krėva (Krewo) was issued by [Jogaila](../characters/jogaila.qmd) at Krėva castle on 14 August 1385 and addressed to the Polish delegation; it was guaranteed by the seals of his brothers Skirgaila, Kaributas and Lengvenis and his cousin [Vytautas](../characters/vytautas.qmd). In exchange for marriage to [Jadwiga](../characters/jadvyga.qmd) he promised to convert Lithuania, to pay 200,000 florins to William of Austria to end her betrothal, to recover Poland's lost lands and free Polish prisoners, and to "attach" (*applicare*) the Lithuanian and Ruthenian lands to the Polish Crown. Historians disagree on *applicare*: it meant incorporation as a province (Koneczny, Łowmiański, Kolankowski), a fief (Adamus, Paszkiewicz) or only a personal union (Šapoka, Ivinskis). Only Jogaila made binding promises, so Kiaupienė argues it was not a final international treaty. The document was found in 1835 in the Kraków chapter archive; no contemporary chronicle mentions the meeting, and Dainauskas's 1975 challenge to its authenticity has found little support (Wikipedia, Union of Krewo).

## What really happened [Saga]

It is signed in the upper hall, directly above the cells where Kęstutis was strangled, one day short of three years after his death. Poles on one side and Lithuanian lords on the other, with a red cloth on the table; the guard spears along the well wall are rimed with white frost in August: the White Silence settles over the realm. Skirgaila, drunk, says he cannot sleep in this castle, it is too quiet. Vytautas, who knows he will have to refuse only once and has decided what to save the refusal for, goes down to the cell, finds the stone where the body lay a different colour, and sees his breath turn to winter. Henė sits on the stairs; his breath does not show.

## Consequences

The graph lists no cause. It leads to [the baptism and coronation at Kraków](ev_krakow_1386.qmd) in February 1386 (the marriage and baptism it promised).
